identity.exchangeName: Nokia Corporation Sponsored American Depositary Shares

risks: AI/cloud order growth can be constrained by optical-component supply and order-to-revenue timing.
Reported operating margin was negative due to accelerated restructuring, creating a meaningful comparable-versus-reported earnings distinction.
Capacity additions can arrive after demand normalizes, shifting a current shortage into utilization risk.
Restructuring creates real near-term cash costs even where comparable profitability improves.
Longer-term customer orders formed during component scarcity may expose Nokia to timing, mix or demand-normalization risk.
Manufacturing expansion intended to relieve optical bottlenecks increases execution and future utilization exposure.
Independent reporting still reflects company-reported quarter data; it corroborates the reported results and demand context but does not independently audit the underlying accounting records.
A raised annual outlook can still be missed if AI/cloud order conversion, component availability, or restructuring execution deteriorates later in 2026.
unknowns: Durability of triple-digit AI & Cloud growth beyond current capacity expansion remains unproven.
Restructuring benefits and cash costs need longitudinal validation.
How much current AI/cloud order growth is durable beyond the present capacity-constrained build cycle remains unproven.
Realized margins on the current AI/cloud order wave and post-restructuring cost savings require longitudinal confirmation.
Durability of AI/cloud order conversion beyond the current capacity-constrained build cycle remains unproven.
Post-Q2 realized margins and cash restructuring costs require later-period validation.
contradictions: Comparable operating margin improved to 9.0% while reported operating margin declined to -1.0% because restructuring accelerated; underwriting should preserve both views.
Underlying comparable profitability improved while reported profitability was negative because restructuring was accelerated.

The prior issuer evidence records comparable margin improvement alongside negative reported margin from restructuring; this Reuters source corroborates comparable-profit strength but does not independently resolve the comparable-versus-reported accounting distinction.
